G0: When solving problems with multiple base constraints, prioritize generating candidates in the base with fewer palindromic possibilities to reduce computational overhead.
G1: In geometric problems involving segment constraints, explicitly validate relationships between segments and their coverage regions to prevent misinterpretation.
G2: In problems involving cyclic quadrilaterals, explicitly verify the positions of all points relative to the circle's center and the given geometric constraints to avoid ambiguous solutions.
G3: Leverage congruent faces and symmetry in disphenoids to simplify volume and area calculations using vector algebra or coordinate geometry.
G4: When solving geometric angle constraints, validate derived angle relationships against each other to ensure consistency with the problem's symmetry and constraints.
G5: In prime factorization scenarios, cross-verify each component's contribution to the total sum of exponents to ensure accuracy in calculations involving perfect squares or divisibility conditions.
G6: For overlapping set problems, cross-validate inclusion-exclusion equations against total population constraints to ensure logical consistency and prevent under/overcounting.
G7: For modular arithmetic with large numbers, validate intermediate steps for divisibility by the modulus to prevent incorrect reductions and maintain accuracy.
G8: For products over roots of unity, recognize that the product of a polynomial evaluated at all roots of a cyclotomic polynomial can often be simplified by exploiting the polynomial's symmetry and known identities, such as the resultant of the polynomials involved.
G9: In combinatorial selections with overlapping constraints, explicitly account for all permutations of distinct elements to ensure comprehensive coverage of favorable outcomes.
G10: In symmetric optimization problems, cross-validate solutions against non-symmetric cases to confirm the global maximum and avoid premature convergence.
G11: For prime difference problems, systematically explore all valid prime combinations rather than restricting to specific patterns or edge cases.
G12: In problems with numerical constraints, cross-validate co-primality checks and modular reductions using alternative methods to ensure robustness.
G13: For problems requiring dual-base palindromicity, cross-validate intermediate conversions using modular arithmetic to ensure accuracy and prevent premature elimination of valid candidates.
G14: In problems involving circular arrangements with geometric constraints, always verify that rotational symmetries are properly addressed to avoid overcounting or undercounting configurations.
G15: In problems requiring division within modular arithmetic, always verify that the divisor and modulus are coprime to ensure the existence of a modular inverse.
G16: In constrained optimization, systematically explore all possible variable configurations (including asymmetric ones) to prevent premature termination of the solution process.
G17: In problems involving multiple angle conditions (e.g., equal angles from different cevians), systematically cross-validate the derived relationships using both coordinate geometry and vector analysis to ensure consistency across all constraints.
G18: When solving problems with parity constraints in combinatorial arrangements, explicitly model the constraints as assignments to distinct parity classes (odd/even positions) to ensure valid configurations.
G19: To prevent undercounting, ensure that all possible configurations of prime differences are evaluated systematically, including wrap-around cases and non-linear sequences, to capture the full range of valid triangles.
